newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi MPs ratify power accord with four states.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi MPs ratify power accord with four states.

text.p: Iraq's National Assembly has ratified an agreement allowing four Arab countries and Turkey to link up in a common power grid, state-run newspapers said on Tuesday.

Iraq, Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Turkey signed accords in Baghdad in 1994 to push ahead with the $450 million worth project which will not include Iraq until U.N. Gulf War trade sanctions against Baghdad are lifted.
Al-Qadissiya paper said MPs endorsed the agreement "after it was discussed thoroughly by oil, energy and minerals committees at the National Assembly".

The Kuwait-based Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development and the Jeddah-based Islamic Development Bank have pledged to finance 80 percent of the project, with the rest coming from local governments.
The project's $340 million first stage will connect Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Turkey within one network. A $110 million second phase will link the Syrian network with Iraq and eventually Turkey.
The papers said the project "will realise a lot of benefits to these countries including the increase of their electricity reserve and the exchange of power during emergencies".
